From: Tom Green <procurement@mediflow.com>

Cc: Sara Patel <finance@mediflow.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Net60 proposal + VAT handling question

Hi Markus,

We reviewed the onboarding terms for the upcoming pilot and have a couple of asks from procurement/finance before we sign the SOW. Our preference is Net60 given the internal payment cycles for pilot vendors. Two specific items: 1) a modest holdback on the final invoice until usage reconciliation (we typically do 15–20%); and 2) clarity on how Redwood will invoice VAT across our EU entities (Mediflow Ltd vs Mediflow Europe GmbH) so we can route to the correct ledger.

Can your team propose a staggered invoice schedule that fits Net60 while still protecting Redwood on the initial ramp? We want to avoid delaying the pilot start but need predictable cashflow mapping.

Thanks — I can loop in procurement counsel if helpful.

Tom
Procurement Manager
Mediflow Inc.

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Tom Green <procurement@mediflow.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Net60 proposal + VAT handling question

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a working draft (proposed_schedule_v2.xlsx) with two options so you can pick the cadence that best matches Mediflow's cashflow:

Option A (balanced):
- Invoice 1 on start: 40% (Net60)
- Invoice 2 at 30 days: 35% (Net60)
- Final reconciliation at 60 days: 25% (holdback applied)

Option B (front-loaded to accelerate delivery):
- Invoice 1 on start: 60%
- Invoice 2 at 30 days: 30%
- Final reconciliation at 60 days: 10% holdback

Our standard holdback is 10% for pilots under $150k; a 15–20% holdback is higher than normal but we can accommodate up to 15% with a brief credit review.

On VAT routing: we included a one-page VAT entity matrix (vat_entity_matrix.pdf) that maps invoice flows depending on which legal entity is purchasing. Quick notes: if Mediflow Europe GmbH signs the SOW, Redwood will issue invoices with EU VAT where required; if Mediflow Ltd (UK) signs, we will follow the UK VAT rules and potentially reverse-charge when applicable. If you can confirm the billing entity and VAT ID we’ll lock the route.

Action items for you:
- Confirm preferred option (A or B) and desired holdback percentage
- Confirm billing/legal entity and VAT ID for invoices
- Provide PO timing estimate so we can schedule the first invoice

Looping in Kimberly and Naomi to help on credit/terms and Marissa for contract amendment.

—Markus
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Tom — quick note from Finance: Net60 is workable for this pilot but we'll need either: 1) a PO covering the first two invoices on signature, or 2) a parent company guarantee for Net60 with a reduced holdback.

If Mediflow can move to Net45 we can waive the standard 2% scheduling fee we apply for extended collections. As Markus noted, 10% holdback is our baseline; we can move to 12–15% only with internal credit approval.

Naomi — can you run a light credit check on Mediflow once Tom confirms entity details?

Kimberly

Thanks all. Two responses from Finance side: first, Mediflow can confirm the buying entity will be Mediflow Europe GmbH (VAT DE123456789). Second, we are open to Net45 rather than Net60 if Redwood can reduce the holdback to 5% provided we agree to quarterly usage reconciliation and a final true-up at contract month 6. That helps our cashflow while giving you a timely settlement rhythm.

On the VAT point, we expect reverse-charge for inter-company transactions inside the EU where applicable — happy to share our tax counsel contact if you want an explicit confirmation.

Sara Patel
Head of Finance, Mediflow Inc.
